subject: Overlaying scatter plot and mean plot

messages.author: bcb52a2d8001a6d1
messages.subject: Overlaying scatter plot and mean plot
parts:
Hi,

I have a basic mean and sd plot.

dfsumm <- data.frame(x=1:3, mean=c(4,5,7), sd=c(1,1,2))
ggplot(dfsumm, aes(x, mean))+
geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd, ymax=mean+sd))+geom_point()

How do I overlay a jittered scattered plot using a 2nd color?

Example data frame:
df <- data.frame(t=c(1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3), val=c(3.9,4,4.1,4.9,5,5.1,6.9,7,7.1))

Troy

messages.author: 68b661fcb57b94a9
messages.subject: Re: Overlaying scatter plot and mean plot
parts:
Use stat_summary to calculate the mean and sd from the data - if you do this, then plotting the data itself will be just a matter of adding geom_jitter().

It'd be even easier to just use geom_boxplot along with geom_jitter().

On 16 December 2010 14:57, Dennis Murphy <djm...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi:

In addition to Erik's answer, I prefer to rein in the jittering, something like the following:

# Your original code:

dfsumm <- data.frame(x=1:3, mean=c(4,5,7), sd=c(1,1,2))
ggplot(dfsumm, aes(x, mean))+

geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd, ymax=mean+sd), width = 0.5)+geom_point()

# I tightened the width of the error bars in the previous line.
# Generated more data to illustrate my point about tightening the jitter...
df <- data.frame(tt = rep(1:3, each = 40),
           val = round(rnorm(120, m = rep(c(4, 5, 7), each = 40))))


ggplot(dfsumm, aes(x, mean))+
 geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd, ymax=mean+sd), width = 0.5, size = 1) +
 geom_point(size = 3) +
 geom_jitter(aes(tt, val), data = df, colour = I("red"),
                   position = position_jitter(width = 0.05))

I added the position argument to Erik's geom_jitter() suggestion to exert control over the extent of the jittering and played around with other arguments such as thickness of the error bars (size = 1) and size of the center points (size = 3 in geom_point()). This should give you some ideas how to customize your plot.

HTH,
Dennis
